audience: Kilo, OpenCode, Pi, and future harness users
engineers who want observable agent behavior and evidence-backed verification
problem: A strong model can still ship brittle work when the surrounding harness rushes into edits, skips research, guesses while tools are running, loses state during compaction or handoff, or stops without checking the result.
solution: Study local ChatGPT Work behavior as reference evidence, model the useful decisions as a harness-neutral protocol, and project that protocol through adapters with explicit provenance, UX, action planning, verification, recovery, and outcome gates.
mechanism: separate ChatGPT Work from other Codex surfaces
measure behavior, UX, research gates, continuity, and task outcomes
define a canonical evidence and semantic-event boundary
project the protocol through Kilo, OpenCode, Pi, and future adapters
evaluate semantic traces and observable outcomes without requiring exact tool sequences

evidence.claim: The repository treats local ChatGPT Work transcripts as the process reference.
The repository has written a Codex-imitate mode and paired Kilo/OpenCode prototype modes.
A process scorer checks look-first, wait/send order, writes, and post-edit verification.
Matched-task replay across long Work threads is still in progress.
The repository now has an owner-review planning package for a harness-agnostic behavior protocol, provenance boundary, UX research, action planning, continuity, adapters, and verifiers.
The protocol implementation, canonical event normalizer, and Pi adapter do not exist yet.

boundaries: This is not a SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, Harbor, or public coding-exam project.
Raw JSONL, SQLite, prompts, transcript bodies, credentials, and user artifacts stay out of Git.
ChatGPT Work behavior is reference evidence, not a literal sequence every harness must copy.
A process score is not the same as reliable task outcome.
The protocol is a wrapper and workflow contract, not a new Codex clone.
Kilo and OpenCode are adapters/examples; Pi and future harnesses are part of the long-term boundary.
The current modes and scorer are preserved prototypes until the owner accepts the reset package.
